parsed.explanation: This division sits under a contested parent regime whose traveler-facing exposures are real but scattered: foreign passports are normally accepted (X markers recognized until expiry), yet entry screening applies 'reasonable doubt' sex scrutiny with possible fraud findings, allied governments issue advisories, and foreigners have been detained over visa issues — a universal-exposure layer every visitor carries. National facility/custody harms documented elsewhere do not reach this division, which adds its own mitigations: no bathroom ban or criminal trigger, no care ban (governor vetoed restrictions), an executive order protecting state services, municipal nondiscrimination coverage, SRS-based birth-certificate amendment, recognized marriage, and a 2026 external assessment placing it in the low-risk group. Custody placement and a care-access pause under national funding pressure remain open questions, not exposures. Rule-of-law courts have blocked several hostile national orders. The entry/document exposure keeps it below 0.75–0.85 anchors, but the division's documented acceptance and absence of local restrictions place it in reduced risk at 0.70.
